text:
The knee-jerk reflex uses a stretch receptor in the thigh muscle, one sensory neurone and one motor neurone, with no relay neurone between them.
How many synapses does this reflex arc have inside the spinal cord?
solution: The sensory neurone synapses directly onto the motor neurone in the spinal cord: one synapse. The motor neurone's junction with the muscle is outside the central nervous system. A reflex with a relay neurone, like pulling a hand from a hot object, has two synapses in the cord.

text: Which of these molecules is built from the greatest number of different chemical elements?
solution: A nucleotide has a phosphate group (P), a sugar (C, H, O) and a nitrogenous base (N): five elements. Glucose, triglycerides and cellulose contain only C, H and O, and water only H and O.

text:
Which of these homeostatic responses are controlled through the hypothalamus?
1 sweating when the body is too hot
2 releasing less ADH when the blood is too dilute
3 releasing insulin when the blood glucose concentration rises
solution: The hypothalamus is the body's thermostat and also senses the water potential of the blood, controlling ADH release from the pituitary. Insulin release needs no brain: the beta cells of the pancreas detect the glucose concentration themselves and respond directly. 1 and 2 only.

text:
Shortly after a meal, which row names a vessel carrying blood with a very high concentration of oxygen, and a vessel carrying blood with the highest concentration of glucose absorbed from the gut?

| | very high oxygen | highest absorbed glucose |
|---|---|---|
| row 1 | pulmonary artery | hepatic vein |
| row 2 | vena cava | hepatic portal vein |
| row 3 | pulmonary artery | hepatic portal vein |
| row 4 | pulmonary vein | renal vein |
| row 5 | pulmonary vein | hepatic portal vein |
solution: The pulmonary vein carries blood just oxygenated in the lungs. Glucose absorbed in the small intestine goes straight to the liver in the hepatic portal vein, before the liver stores much of it; the hepatic vein carries blood after that. The pulmonary artery and vena cava carry deoxygenated blood.

text: Which enzyme carries out transcription, joining RNA nucleotides in an order set by a DNA template?
solution: RNA polymerase reads the template strand and links complementary RNA nucleotides into mRNA. DNA polymerase copies DNA during replication, ligase seals DNA backbones, reverse transcriptase makes DNA from RNA, and ribosomes carry out translation.

text:
A cross produces offspring with four phenotypes in the ratio 1 : 1 : 1 : 1.
Which of the following could be true?
1 Two genes were studied, each with two alleles.
2 One parent was heterozygous for both genes and the other homozygous recessive for both.
3 Both parents were heterozygous for both genes.
solution: Four phenotypes from a cross fits two genes with two alleles each (1). The test cross AaBb x aabb gives AaBb, Aabb, aaBb and aabb in equal numbers: 1 : 1 : 1 : 1 (2). Two double heterozygotes give 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 instead (3 wrong). 1 and 2 only.

text: A skin cell and a liver cell are taken from the same healthy person. Which of the following would be the SAME in both?
options: the base sequence of their nuclear DNA
solution: Both cells come from the same zygote by mitosis, so their nuclear DNA is identical. They differ because they express different genes, so their mRNA, proteins and shapes differ.

text: Which statement about human gametes is NOT correct?
options: A sperm carries either an X or a Y chromosome.
An egg always carries an X chromosome.
They are made by mitosis in the testes and ovaries.
solution: Gametes are made by MEIOSIS, which halves the chromosome number from 46 to 23 (haploid). The mother has XX, so every egg has an X; the father has XY, so a sperm has either. Mitosis would keep 46 chromosomes.

text: Which statement about nerve impulses in humans is NOT true?
options: They travel along neurones as electrical signals.
They usually act faster than hormones.
They cross synapses by means of chemical neurotransmitters.
They are carried to their target organs in the blood plasma.
solution: Hormones travel in the blood; nerve impulses travel along neurones, as action potentials, to a precise target. Nervous responses are fast and brief, and they cross synapses chemically.

text:
Which of these processes move substances DOWN their concentration gradient?
1 diffusion
2 facilitated diffusion
3 active transport
solution: Simple and facilitated diffusion are both passive: they go from high to low concentration, the second through channel or carrier proteins. Active transport uses carrier proteins and ATP to move substances AGAINST the gradient. 1 and 2 only.

text: Which cross can produce offspring with the genotype aabb?
solution: An aabb child needs an a and a b from EACH parent. AaBb can give ab and aabb gives only ab, so aabb is possible (1 in 4). In the others one parent is AA or BB and must pass on a dominant allele, so aabb is impossible.

text: Why are many bacterial infections becoming harder to treat with antibiotics?
options: Bacteria learn to avoid antibiotics during an infection.
Bacteria carrying mutations that give resistance survive treatment and pass the resistance on.
Antibiotics lose their strength inside the body over the years.
Viruses carry resistance genes into human cells.
solution: This is natural selection. Random mutations make a few bacteria resistant; the antibiotic kills the rest, and the survivors multiply, so resistance spreads (and can pass between bacteria on plasmids). Patients do not become resistant, and bacteria do not learn; overuse and unfinished courses speed the selection up.

text:
A newly made protein is to be placed in the cell surface membrane. In which order does it pass through these structures?
1 Golgi apparatus
2 vesicle
3 rough endoplasmic reticulum
4 cell surface membrane
solution: The protein is made on ribosomes of the rough ER and enters it, travels to the Golgi apparatus to be modified and sorted, and leaves in a vesicle that fuses with the cell surface membrane, leaving the protein in it. The Golgi always comes after the ER.

text:
Which of the following increase when the parasympathetic nervous system is dominant ("rest and digest")?
1 heart rate
2 movement of food along the gut
3 secretion of saliva
solution: The parasympathetic system promotes digestion: it increases gut movement (peristalsis) and saliva flow. It SLOWS the heart, through the vagus nerve; speeding the heart is the job of the sympathetic system and adrenaline. 2 and 3 only.

text:
Which of the following statements about the O-H bonds INSIDE a water molecule is/are correct?
1 They are much stronger than the hydrogen bonds between water molecules.
2 They are polar.
3 They break when water boils.
solution: The O-H bonds are covalent and about twenty times stronger than hydrogen bonds (1). Oxygen is far more electronegative than hydrogen, so they are polar, which is what makes hydrogen bonding possible (2). Boiling separates molecules by breaking hydrogen bonds; the water molecules themselves stay whole (3 wrong).

text: Which formula could NOT belong to a saturated, open-chain carboxylic acid?
solution: These acids fit \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n}O_2}\): the C=O in the COOH group costs two hydrogens compared with an alkane. \(\mathrm{C_4H_{10}O_2}\) has two hydrogens too many for that (it fits a diol such as butane-1,4-diol). The others fit: ethanoic, propanoic, pentanoic and hexanoic acid.

text:
Which of the following statements about dissolving in water is/are correct?
1 Some ionic compounds, such as calcium carbonate, are insoluble in water.
2 Some covalent compounds, such as sucrose, dissolve in water.
3 Gases usually become less soluble in water as the temperature rises.
solution: Not every ionic solid dissolves: the lattice of calcium carbonate is too strong. Polar covalent molecules that can hydrogen-bond, like sucrose, dissolve well. Gases escape as water warms, which is why warm water holds less oxygen. All three are correct.

text:
Which substances are the REDUCING agents in these three reactions?
\(\mathrm{2Na + Cl_2 \rightarrow 2NaCl}\)
\(\mathrm{Zn + Cu^{2+} \rightarrow Zn^{2+} + Cu}\)
\(\mathrm{Cl_2 + 2Br^- \rightarrow 2Cl^- + Br_2}\)
solution: A reducing agent gives electrons away and is itself oxidised. Sodium goes from 0 to +1, zinc from 0 to +2, and bromide from -1 to 0 in bromine. Chlorine and \(\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}\) gain electrons, so they are the oxidising agents.

text: Which statement about lithium, sodium and potassium is NOT correct?
options: They react with water to form hydroxides.
They form ions with a 1+ charge.
They are soft enough to cut with a knife.
Their reactivity increases down the group.
They are all denser than water.
solution: Lithium, sodium and potassium all float on water (densities about 0.53, 0.97 and 0.86 g/cm3). The other statements are typical Group 1 properties: a single outer electron, lost more easily down the group, and weak metallic bonding that makes them soft.

text:
How many hydrogen atoms are in 0.32 g of methane, (mathrm{CH_4})?
[Relative atomic masses: H = 1; C = 12; Avogadro constant = (6.0 	imes 10^{23} mathrm{mol^{-1}})]
solution: (M_r) of methane = 16, so 0.32 g is 0.020 mol of molecules. Each has four hydrogens: 0.080 mol of H atoms = (0.080 	imes 6.0 	imes 10^{23} = 4.8 	imes 10^{22}). (1.2 	imes 10^{22}) counts molecules, not hydrogen atoms.

text:
How many electrons does each ion in magnesium oxide have?
[Atomic numbers: O = 8; Mg = 12]
solution: Magnesium loses two electrons to form \(\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}\): 12 - 2 = 10. Oxygen gains two to form \(\mathrm{O^{2-}}\): 8 + 2 = 10. Both end with the neon arrangement.

text: Which is correct about the first and second ionisation energies of magnesium?
options: first: endothermic; second: smaller than the first
first: endothermic; second: endothermic and larger than the first
solution: Pulling an electron away from a nucleus always takes energy, so every ionisation energy is endothermic. The second electron leaves a 1+ ion that holds its remaining electrons more tightly, so the second ionisation energy is larger (about 1450 against 740 kJ/mol for magnesium).

text:
Consider these reactions:
\(\mathrm{C_2H_4 + Br_2 \rightarrow C_2H_4Br_2}\)
\(\mathrm{HCl + NaOH \rightarrow NaCl + H_2O}\)
\(\mathrm{C_2H_5OH \rightarrow C_2H_4 + H_2O}\)
Which type of reaction is NOT shown?
solution: Bromine adds across ethene's double bond (addition); an acid and a base form a salt and water (neutralisation); ethanol loses water to form ethene, which is both elimination and dehydration. No atom or group is swapped for another, so there is no substitution.

text:
Which rows correctly state whether the compound fizzes, giving carbon dioxide, when added to sodium carbonate solution?

| | compound | gives carbon dioxide |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | ethanoic acid | yes |
| 2 | ethanol | no |
| 3 | ethanal | yes |
solution: Carboxylic acids are acidic enough to react with carbonates and release carbon dioxide, so ethanoic acid fizzes (row 1 correct). Alcohols and aldehydes are not acidic, so neither ethanol nor ethanal does: row 2 is correct and row 3 is wrong. This is the standard test for a COOH group.

text: Which is NOT the correct formula of a calcium compound?
solution: Calcium forms \(\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}\), so it needs two 1- ions such as nitrate: calcium nitrate is \(\mathrm{Ca(NO_3)_2}\). Carbonate and sulfate are 2-, so one of each; phosphate is 3-, so three calciums balance two phosphates.

subject: Mathematics
text: For which values of \(x\) are both \(x^2 > 4\) and \(3 - x > 0\) true?
solution: \(x^2 > 4\) holds outside -2 and 2: \(x < -2\) or \(x > 2\). \(3 - x > 0\) means \(x < 3\). Combining: all of \(x < -2\) survives, and of \(x > 2\) only \(2 < x < 3\). Forgetting the negative branch gives just \(2 < x < 3\).

subject: Physics
text:
A student finds the specific latent heat of vaporisation of water by keeping water boiling with a heater of known power and measuring how much boils away.
Which of the following does the student NOT need?
options: the time for which the water boils
the temperature of the water before it was heated
the mass of water when timing starts
the mass of water when timing stops
solution: Latent heat = energy / mass boiled away. Energy = power x time, and the mass boiled away is the difference between the masses at the start and end of timing, while the water is already boiling. How cold the water was before it reached 100 °C does not enter the calculation.

subject: Physics
text:
Water is boiling steadily at 100 °C and atmospheric pressure. Which of the following statements is/are correct?
1 It absorbs energy but its temperature stays the same.
2 Hydrogen bonds between water molecules are broken.
3 O-H bonds inside the water molecules are broken.
solution: During a change of state the energy goes into separating molecules (latent heat), not into raising the temperature (1). Separating water molecules means breaking the hydrogen bonds between them (2). The molecules themselves survive as \(\mathrm{H_2O}\) in the steam (3 wrong).

subject: Physics
text:
A coil of superconducting wire has zero electrical resistance. A steady current flows in it.
Which statement is correct?
options: No magnetic field forms around the coil.
A large voltage is needed to keep the current flowing.
Energy is lost from the wire as heat at a rate of \(I^2R\).
A magnetic field forms around the coil, but no heat is produced in the wire.
solution: Heating is \(I^2R\), which is zero when R is zero, and with no resistance no voltage is needed to keep a steady current going. But any current produces a magnetic field, which is why superconducting coils are used for the strong magnets in MRI scanners.

subject: Physics
text: Which one of the following IS a vector quantity?
solution: A vector has a direction as well as a size. Momentum is mass x velocity, and velocity has a direction, so momentum does too. Kinetic energy, temperature, mass and power have size only: they are scalars.

subject: Mathematics
text: Simplify \(\ln(x^3y^2) - 3\ln(xy) + \ln y\).
solution: Expand: \(3\ln x + 2\ln y - 3\ln x - 3\ln y + \ln y\). The \(\ln x\) terms cancel, and \(2 - 3 + 1 = 0\), so the \(\ln y\) terms cancel too: the expression is 0 for all positive \(x\) and \(y\).

subject: Mathematics
text:
In a class, exactly \(\tfrac{3}{4}\) of the students play a sport and exactly \(\tfrac{1}{2}\) learn a musical instrument.
What is the range of possible values for the fraction of the class who do both?
solution: At most, every musician also plays a sport: \(\tfrac{1}{2}\). At least, the two groups overlap as little as possible, but together they make \(\tfrac{5}{4}\) of a class, so at least \(\tfrac{3}{4} + \tfrac{1}{2} - 1 = \tfrac{1}{4}\) must do both. \(\tfrac{3}{8}\) is the value only if the two are independent.

subject: Mathematics
text: Which of these points lies at a different distance from the line (y = x + 1) than the other four?
solution: The distance from \((p, q)\) to \(x - y + 1 = 0\) is \(\dfrac{|p - q + 1|}{\sqrt{2}}\). The numerators: (0, 3) gives 2, (2, 1) gives 2, (4, 3) gives 2, (1, 0) gives 2, but (3, 3) gives 1. So (3, 3) is the odd one out.

subject: Physics
text:
A 60 kg woman puts her whole weight on one stiletto heel, whose tip has an area of 1.0 cm².
What pressure does the heel exert on the floor?
[Take \(g = 10\) N/kg.]
solution: Weight = 60 x 10 = 600 N. Area: 1.0 cm² = \(1.0 \times 10^{-4}\ \text{m}^2\) (a centimetre is \(10^{-2}\) m, so a square centimetre is \(10^{-4}\)). Pressure = 600 / \(10^{-4}\) = \(6.0 \times 10^{6}\) Pa, more than an elephant's foot exerts.
